visualLanguage: design_system/public/PUBLIC_UI.md, built from components/site/v3. THIS FILE BINDS: requiredComponents is what stops a page silently losing a section, and ci:mockup-parity reads it with or without a mockup.
competitiveTarget: Beat five-step contact wizards and generic 'get in touch' pages: one-screen V3Ask, local brokers with real phone numbers as doors, FAQ as disclosures.
note: Live 2026-09-03 leftover. Order is Breadcrumb, Quiet (H1 Call, text, or write), V3Doors (call/text, email, book), V3Ask (one screen, every field, one button — not the old five-step sheet), V3Ledger (who answers), V3Answers (CONTACT_FAQ_ITEMS as disclosures), Footer. Consent checkbox is padded to --v3-tap on this route without changing SMS_CONSENT_TEXT. tasteReview is withheld until a separate evaluator grades the rendered page (design_system/public/TASTE.md). Do not invent a score.

tasteReview.beats: Beats a Zillow/Realtor.com agent card on trust transparency: a named Oregon license number and a sourced, expandable ratings methodology ('SOURCE Google reviews' / 'how we calculate this') rather than a generic, unlinked review badge.
tasteReview.dullest: The office row — a pin icon, a static address, and an arrow with no map, photo, or live data attached; next to the broker row's rating bar and expandable methodology it reads as pure filler text.
tasteReview.verdict: This is a real step up from the prior build — a photo, a sourced rating with a disclosure toggle, and a location line replace what was pure eyebrow-heading-paragraph text. But the page is still named for an action ('Call, text, or write') that isn't visible on either device without scrolling, and the fold spends more of its space on hairlines and blank cream than on anything a visitor can do or look at. Fix the fold before polishing anything else.

defects.finding: The headline reads 'Call, text, or write' but no actionable call/text/email/schedule control appears in either captured viewport — the row is entirely off-screen at 375x812, and at 1440x900 only its four column labels ('CALL', 'TEXT', 'EMAIL', 'SCHEDULE') peek in at the very bottom edge with nothing else legible.
defects.fix: Bring at least one real action (a phone/text link, or the first CTA cell) above the fold so the headline's promise is backed by something clickable without scrolling.

defects.finding: On desktop there is a large dead band of plain cream between 'The office' row and the thick hairline that opens the next block, with no image, map, or secondary visual filling it — the single 60px-ish broker headshot is the only departure from navy-on-cream text anywhere in the fold.
defects.fix: Either tighten the vertical rhythm so the CTA row surfaces higher, or use that space for a real visual (office photo, map thumbnail) instead of empty cream.

defects.finding: The location entry is a pin icon, plain address text, and an arrow — visually identical in weight to the broker row above it, with no map thumbnail, photo, or live data (hours, open-now) attached. It is the least distinctive block on the page.
defects.fix: Attach a small static map or office photo, or surface live hours/availability, so the row rewards a look the way the ratings row does.
